cells: IA PATHFINDER  |  TWO PARTS
Students plan a feasible investigation first, then move to completing it.
PROJECT STRUCTURE
1  ·  PLANNING THE IA  ↗
2  ·  COMPLETING THE IA  ↗

PLANNING FLOWCHART
Choose aim → Who is this for? (personal benefit or advice) → IA type/data and feasibility → Maths → Type-specific prediction → WHY? → IF TRUE, what would that mean for this person? (Edit beneficiary) → Revisit mathematics → Review → Personalised planning document.

COMPLETING THE IA  |  REFLECTION THROUGHOUT, SYNTHESIS AT THE END
Students evaluate method choices and mathematical findings AS THEY HAPPEN, including their effect on results, limits and new mathematical direction. The conclusion must NOT repeat graphs/calculations or become a belated evaluation section; it answers the aim, draws together the key evidence, explains meaningful implications for the beneficiary, and proposes relevant future directions (or an unresolved question) without overstating evidence.

AGREED PURPOSE LOOP
During prediction, students revisit the aim and beneficiary, explain the possible impact IF TRUE, and can edit 'Who is it for?' without restarting. The planning PDF/Word retains the latest purpose and hypothetical implication for Completing the IA.

LIMITATION EXAMPLES — RIGHT TIME, RIGHT CONTEXT
Data Collection offers only actual sampling, source and measurement limitations. PMCC, regression, model assumptions or optimisation weaknesses are offered later, when students are using those techniques. Conclusions revisit only limitations the student confirmed.
